newsitem.title: UK: Eurotunnel no change to financial restructure.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel no change to financial restructure.

text.p: Eurotunnel Plc/SA, the Channel Tunnel operator hit by a major fire in a tunnel last year, said on Monday it saw no need to review its financial restructuring plans to cover debt levels of nearly 9.0 billion pounds ($15.05 billion).

It reported that prospects for 1997 looked encouraging, adding that 1996 had seen turnover of around 450 million stg versus 300 million in 1995, with 13 million passengers going through the tunnel last year. That compares with eight million in 1995. Giving an update on the fire, Eurotunnel said that all sections of its tunnel would be repaired and open in June.

Commenting on the fall-out from the fire which led to a main section of a tunnel being closed last year, the group said in its statement: "The board...believes that the November fire should not have any significant effects on the long-term financial performance of the company, nor will there will any need to review the financial restructuring plan which was agreed in principle with representatives from the banking syndicates on October 1, 1996."
The board also postponed the extraordinary shareholders' meeting aimed at securing approval restructuring plan until the end of June from April, when repairs will be completed.
On the fire insurance, the group has received a 34 million stg advance from its insurers for lost revenue. The first instalment of 4.5 million pounds ($7.53 million) was paid in December.
Eurotunnel did not quantify the total impact of the fire damage, which has hit revenues for the Le Shuttle car services and the Eurostar passenger service. ($1=.5979 Pound)
